ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, two congruent equilateral triangles overlap each other in opposite directions, and the corresponding sides are parallel to each other, forming a figure similar to a hexagram. The overlapping region in the middle is a regular hexagon, and there are six congruent small equilateral triangles around it. Reasoning: The perimeter of each large equilateral triangle is 18, so each side length is 18 ÷ 3 = 6. In the regular hexagram division shown in the figure, one side of the large triangle is divided into three equal small line segments: one outer small triangle side, one middle regular hexagon side, and another outer small triangle side. Therefore each side length of the middle regular hexagon is 6 ÷ 3 = 2. A regular hexagon has 6 sides, so the perimeter is 6 × 2 = 12.

method.method_draft: Use the image as a regular hexagram dissection. First read from the picture that the two congruent equilateral triangles are oppositely oriented with parallel sides, forming a central regular hexagon and six congruent small equilateral triangles around it. From the text, each large equilateral triangle has perimeter 18, so each large side is 6. In the hexagram configuration, each side of a large triangle is divided into three equal small segments: an outer small-triangle side, one side of the central hexagon, and another outer small-triangle side. Therefore each side of the central hexagon is 6/3 = 2, and its perimeter is 6 · 2 = 12.

method.method_draft: Set up coordinates based on the image. Read the picture as one equilateral triangle pointing up and an identical one pointing down, with corresponding sides parallel and centered to form the displayed hexagon. From the text, the side length of each triangle is 18/3 = 6. Place the upward triangle with horizontal base and write equations for its three sides; place the downward congruent triangle with the same center and parallel side directions. Solving the intersections of alternating side lines gives the six vertices of the central hexagon. The coordinate differences between adjacent vertices have length 6/3 = 2, so the hexagon perimeter is 6 · 2 = 12.
